Chains.__comment: DEV ONLY. Points at TRON's Nile testnet (not mainnet) so round-trip testing uses free faucet funds, never real money. Verify this endpoint yourself before relying on it.

Blockchain.__comment: DEV ONLY override of Blockchain:Assets for Nile: keeps the mainnet USDT entry (inert on Nile - the contract doesn't exist there) and adds native TRX so a testnet round-trip needs no token contract.

Reconciliation.__comment: Absolute base-unit drift tolerated before a pass is flagged Drift (default 0 = exact). Raise to absorb known transients — a deposit landed on chain but not yet confirmed into the ledger, or a withdrawal broadcast but not yet settled. Never hides drift: the exact value is always recorded on the snapshot. Reconciliation is log-only + Mongo snapshots (collections Reconciliation / ReconciliationHistory); the worker interval is set in Program.cs.

Gateway.__comment: DEV ONLY. Must match launchSettings.json applicationUrl — it is the host part of the payUrl returned by /api/v1/deposit, so a mismatch hands the payer a dead link.

Withdrawal.__comment: DEV ONLY. LiveTron=true wires the REAL TRON build/sign/broadcast against the Nile testnet (Level 3). It needs a THROWAWAY testnet key + a funded hot wallet registered via Treasury:DevHotWallets (below) — never here (§10). See docs/withdrawal-testnet.md. Keep false unless doing a live testnet run; withdrawal then uses the node-free in-memory signer/engine.
Withdrawal.__comment_policies: DEV ONLY: confirmation depth 1 so an in-memory withdrawal (mined at block 0 on the fresh fake chain) confirms + settles immediately. Min/Max/Fee/ApprovalThreshold come from appsettings.json.
Withdrawal.__comment_float: DEV ONLY: seeds the in-memory hot wallet with this on-chain float (base units) so the physical float gate clears and withdrawals send. Default 1,000,000 USDT. Set LOW (or 0) to demo the insufficient-balance park path (status 'insufficient_balance', auto-resumes when the float is raised). No effect under LiveTron=true, which reads the real on-chain balance.
Withdrawal.__comment_screening: Address screening of the payout destination. Off by default: a payout only enters PendingScreening when this is on, so turning it on is a deliberate act. Hold (default) sends an inconclusive verdict to the platform approval queue; Allow lets it through unscreened during a vendor outage. In dev with no MistTrack key the in-memory provider scores everything clean, so the queue drains immediately.

Treasury.__comment: DEV ONLY. Ensures a POOL of hot withdrawal wallets on boot (idempotent, grow-only). Each is a watch-only child of the one platform withdrawal HD wallet — addresses are DERIVED from the dev withdrawal seed (or KeyManagement:DevWithdrawalXpub), never configured here, and no key material lives here (§10). Raise Size to grow the pool; each wallet processes one withdrawal at a time (leased until confirmed). For a live Nile run, set KeyManagement:DevWithdrawalXpub to a real funded xpub in the git-ignored appsettings.Local.json.
Treasury.__comment_cold: DEV ONLY. Registers the cold COLLECTION addresses (public, watch-only — NO key, §10; the cold key stays with the human operator, who signs anything that leaves them). Sweep sends deposits here. Kind picks which class of funds the address collects: Safe (clean sweeps, the default) or Danger (the quarantine address a flagged deposit address is swept into, when Sweep:Screening:Enabled is on). The shipped address is deliberately NOT a valid TRON address: it is refused by the format check, so a fresh clone cannot sweep to a made-up destination and sweeping simply stays inert (the boot log says so). Put real watch-only T-addresses in the git-ignored appsettings.Local.json for a live run. Prod registers them via the staff ops action, not config.

Energy.__comment: DEV ONLY. DevStakingWallets seeds the platform staking (energy) wallet — the delegation SOURCE the sweep energy gate draws from. EMPTY by default (no seeding, no boot warning). To exercise real delegation on Nile testnet: in the git-ignored appsettings.Local.json add an entry { Chain, Address (a funded testnet T-address), SecretReference } plus the throwaway key under KeyManagement:DevSecrets[SecretReference] (64-hex, colon-free key name), and fund the address with faucet TRX to freeze. Prod provisions this via a KMS-backed ops action, never config (§10).

DevSampleData.__comment: DEV ONLY. Seeds a demo portfolio for UI development: 3 merchants with different fees/settlement terms (one frozen), deposit invoices in varied states, credited deposits, and withdrawals in every status a screen must render. Seeds INPUTS only — the real workers produce every deposit/journal/balance, so nothing bypasses the ledger (§14). Needs the in-memory chain (Chains:Tron:Live=false); idempotent (skips if DEMOACME exists). Takes 1-2 minutes to converge. See docs/dev-sample-data.md.

DevSeed.__comment: DEV ONLY. A fixed active test merchant so a signed /api/v1 request works out of the box. SigningSecret is a 64-hex (32-byte) HMAC key — client signs HMAC-SHA256(hexDecode(SigningSecret), "{X-Timestamp}\n{body}"). Override in a git-ignored appsettings.Local.json. Never a real merchant's secret (§10).
DevSeed.Name: Dev Test Merchant
DevSeed.__feeComment: DEV sample pricing (basis points; 100 = 1%) so the round-trip shows a non-zero fee split. Applied to every active asset. Production fees are set per-merchant via PUT /api/v1/ops/merchants/{id}/fees.
DevSeed.__cashOutComment: DEV merchant-withdrawal (earnings cash-out): SettlementAddress is the whitelisted destination for POST /api/v1/merchant-withdraw. MerchantWithdrawalPercentBps caps a single cash-out to a % of available balance (5000 = 50%); 0 = no cap. Production sets these via the Ops staff endpoints (Phase 2).
DevSeed.__settlementComment: DEV merchant settlement period (T+N) in whole days. 0 = T+0 so a fresh deposit is immediately withdrawable and the dev happy path isn't blocked. Set to 1 or 2 to demo the settled-balance gate (a just-confirmed deposit then can't be withdrawn/cashed out until it matures). Max 30. Production sets this via the Ops staff endpoint (Phase 2).

Screening.__comment: Staff-side address screening. ScreenSettlementWallets checks a wallet as it is whitelisted. RescreenSettlementWallets periodically re-checks wallets ALREADY on file, because a verdict is a snapshot and an address clean when approved can be designated later; it FLAGS ONLY and never revokes, since every merchant cash-out already stops for staff audit. Both default OFF and are independent: whitelisting is a handful of calls a month, re-screening is one per merchant per chain per cycle forever. RescreenIntervalHours is only how often a pass LOOKS - Compliance:CacheDays decides how often an address is actually re-screened, so a short interval costs nothing.

KeyManagement.__comment: DEV ONLY. DevSecrets holds PUBLIC xpubs only — never a seed/mnemonic (§10). Default is the published abandon..about BIP-39 vector. To derive production addresses locally, override the xpub in a git-ignored appsettings.Local.json (same key), not here.

Compliance.__comment: Address screening (Platform/Compliance). Enabled=false means every call returns Unavailable WITHOUT contacting a provider — screening is switched on deliberately, never left on by a forgotten key. The thresholds are OURS; the provider only supplies a score, so swapping vendors cannot move our risk appetite. CacheDays is the main lever on provider quota. With no MistTrack key this host uses the in-memory provider, which scores every unstaged address clean — never registered in Production (§10).

MistTrack.__comment: BaseUrl decides sandbox vs live, so the SAME adapter code runs in both. Put a real key in appsettings.Local.json (git-ignored) — never here (§10). Empty key keeps the in-memory provider in Development.

Compliance.__comment_proximity: Proximity rule for INDIRECT exposure, OFF by default (MaxHops 0 disables it). All indirect exposure is otherwise left entirely to the score, which is the safe default and what makes screening usable - but it treats 60% of volume one hop away the same as 0.1% five hops away. When enabled, an indirect finding whose risk type is in AlwaysBlockIndicators, within MaxHops AND at or above MinPercent, is raised to Review. Never to Block: Block stays reserved for a DIRECT designation, which is a legal fact rather than a matter of degree. Both conditions must hold - distance alone would flag almost every address with exchange history. Do not guess these numbers: every screening stores the full provider payload, so measure the hop and percentage distribution of real destinations once volume has run through, and set them from that. Reference point from live data: an ordinary TRX address reads 2.735% at 3 hops.

Screening.__comment: Screening of OUR OWN funded deposit addresses - the only inbound control available, since a transfer cannot be screened in flight and an arrived deposit is never refused (a frozen merchant's deposits still credit the ledger). A provider scores an address from its history, so tainted inflow raises the score of our receiving address. It RECORDS AND FLAGS ONLY; nothing is reversed, withheld or disabled. Enabled is the SCHEDULED pass and defaults off; the manual sweep on the ops host runs regardless. MaxAddressesPerPass is the important control: deposit addresses grow without bound and this shares a quota with the payout gate, which is the control that actually holds money - this pass must never be the reason a payout cannot be screened. IntervalHours is how often it LOOKS; Compliance:CacheDays decides how often an address is really re-screened.
